items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Paul Chambers would be coming to my apartment. “I got a date here is the music can we work on it over here?”

ctx.x: Now, at this same time, you’re still hitting at The Five Spot.

Yet, the days were quite full. Whatever you could slam into your schedule daily. You did many things musically. Paul Chambers, early morning, like you would be up at 10 AM, Paul Chambers would be coming to my apartment. “I got a date here is the music can we work on it over here?” “Well, yeah.” “I already called Clifford Jordan, he’ll be over in a minute.” So, we had a gathering of musicians like that. I would still find time, most of my days were spent with John Coltrane. We were into… It should show through our…

Before we get there, and talking about your time at The Five Spot, I mean, there is a whole collection of all these things that that group did. The Mosaic Set that documents this whole period…But, I’m getting from this. That now you’re getting this theoretical training, or dealing with Benny and all that he is giving to you, but you’re really not getting an outlet for your work at that point.
